citation: "The Last War Dance." Chicagology, transcribing later published recollections of 18 August 1835 in Chicago.
note: CITED HERE FOR ONE NARROW PURPOSE AND NO OTHER: it is the only statement reached that fixes the state of the two branch bridges within weeks of the scene date. Its account of 18 August 1835 has a procession cross 'the North Branch bridge' and then move 'south along West Water street (now Canal street), in front of the "Green Tree Tavern" and "Wolf's Point Tavern" to the log raft bridge across the south branch' — which places the crossing, proves the bridge was standing six and a half weeks after 1835-07-01, and shows it carrying a crowd, against Andreas's 'useless for teams' of 1833. THE SUBJECT OF THIS PAGE IS THE FINAL REMOVAL OF THE POTAWATOMI FROM CHICAGO, which AGENTS.md places under the project's standing constraint. Nothing in this dataset depicts, stages or narrates that event, and nothing derived from this source goes beyond the built environment: bridge standing, bridge load-bearing, route of the streets. The page is a later compilation of recollections, unfootnoted, and is tiered accordingly.
